'''Stefano Vitale''' (born 1951, Naples, Italy) is an Italian physicist and a retired professor of [[experimental physics]] at the [[University of Trento]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stefano Vitale {{!}} Teaching {{!}} University of Trento|url=https://webapps.unitn.it/du/en/Persona/PER0000345/Didattica|access-date=2021-09-30|website=webapps.unitn.it}}</ref> He is known for his scientific contributions<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stefano Vitale {{!}} Publications {{!}} University of Trento|url=https://webapps.unitn.it/du/en/Persona/PER0000345/Pubblicazioni|access-date=2021-09-30|website=webapps.unitn.it}}</ref> in the field of [[gravitational wave]] (GW) research  and the successful management of international scientific projects.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – LISA Pathfinder lead scientist awarded prestigious prize|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa-pathfinder/-/lisa-pathfinder-lead-scientist-awarded-prestigious-prize|access-date=2021-09-30|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref>

In particular he has been the co-Principal Investigator of the cryogenic, resonant-bar GW detector [[AURIGA]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=The AURIGA members|url=http://www.auriga.lnl.infn.it/auriga/people/AURIGA_people.html|access-date=2021-09-30|website=www.auriga.lnl.infn.it}}</ref>  and the Principal Investigator of the LISA Technology Package,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stefano Vitale, LISA Pathfinder Principal investigator University of Trente|url=https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2005/04/Stefano_Vitale_LISA_Pathfinder_Principal_investigator_University_of_Trente|access-date=2021-10-06|website=www.esa.int|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – LISA Technology Package|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa-pathfinder/-/55633-lisa-technology-package|access-date=2021-11-25|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref> the sole instrument of [[European Space Agency|ESA]]´s [[LISA Pathfinder]] mission.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – Seeing the Universe through gravitational waves|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa-pathfinder/-/56942-seeing-the-universe-through-gravitational-waves|access-date=2021-09-30|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref> He continues to do scientific research and is Co-lead of the international LISA Consortium.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LISA Consortium {{!}} Lisamission.org|url=https://www.lisamission.org/articles/lisa-consortium|access-date=2021-10-01|website=www.lisamission.org}}</ref> LISA, the [[Laser Interferometer Space Antenna]], is the future [[Gravitational-wave observatory|gravitational wave-observatory]] in space, led by ESA.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – LISA|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa/|access-date=2021-10-01|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref>

Vitale has served on many different committees.<ref>{{Cite web|title=L'Istituto – Accademici – Stefano Vitale|url=http://www.istitutoveneto.it/flex/cm/pages/ServeBLOB.php/L/IT/IDPagina/1597|access-date=2021-11-11|website=www.istitutoveneto.it|language=it}}</ref> In particular he has been the chair of the [[Fundamental interaction|Fundamental Physics]] Advisory group<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESO – participants|url=https://www.eso.org/sci/meetings/2003/esaeso-2003/participants.html|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.eso.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Il fisico americano Kip Thorne a Trento|url=https://www.esa.int/Space_in_Member_States/Italy/Il_fisico_americano_Kip_Thorne_a_Trento|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.esa.int|language=en}}</ref> of Science Directorate of ESA, and the chair of ESA's Science Programme Committee,<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – LISA Pathfinder lead scientist awarded prestigious prize|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa-pathfinder/-/lisa-pathfinder-lead-scientist-awarded-prestigious-prize|access-date=2021-10-05|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref> the delegate body that steers the mandatory agency science program.

== Career ==
Vitale received his [[Laurea]] in Physics at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] (now Università degli Studi di Roma "[[Sapienza University of Rome|La Sapienza]]") in 1976 and was a research fellow at the University of Trento from 1977 to 1979. From 1980 to 1985 he was appointed Assistant Professor for [[Condensed matter physics]] at University of Trento, after which he became Associate Professor of Physics there. Since 1994 he was full Professor of Physics at the University of Trento and served 2001 to 2004 also as Deputy Rector (Prorettore Vicario). He retired from his Professorship on 30 September 2021.

In 1992, Vitale was visiting professor at the Department of Physics at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]] and from 1997 to 1998 he also was Visiting Scholar at the University of California at Berkeley and [[Stanford University]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stefano Vitale|url=https://einstein.stanford.edu/STEP/people/collaborators/data/svitale.html|access-date=2021-10-01|website=einstein.stanford.edu}}</ref> in California. Since 1985, Vitale is a research associate at the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] (INFN).

During his career, Vitale served on many national and international academic bodies, managing scientific projects and communities and advocating for basic and applied research.<ref>{{Cite web|title=L'Istituto – Accademici – Stefano Vitale|url=http://www.istitutoveneto.it/flex/cm/pages/ServeBLOB.php/L/IT/IDPagina/1597|access-date=2021-10-01|website=www.istitutoveneto.it|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=International Astronomical Union {{!}} IAU|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/18802/|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.iau.org}}</ref>

== Experimental gravitational wave research ==
Vitale got involved in experimental gravitational wave research in the late 1980s. From 1988 to 2001 and then again from 2005 until his retirement in 2021, he was Head of the Laboratory for Experimental Gravitation at the Department of Physics of the University of Trento where cutting edge technologies for [[Gravitational-wave observatory|gravitational wave observatories]] were developed and tested.

From 1989 to 2003 Vitale was the co-Principal Investigator of the cryogenic, resonant-bar GW detector [[AURIGA]], by the Italian Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, based in [[Legnaro]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=AURIGA Home Page|url=http://www.auriga.lnl.infn.it/|access-date=2021-11-24|website=www.auriga.lnl.infn.it|archive-date=6 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101006215119/http://www.auriga.lnl.infn.it/}}</ref> AURIGA has been the most sensitive of this kind of detectors,<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Ciufolini|first1=Ignazio|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v0pSfo8vrtsC&dq=AURIGA+detector&pg=PA133|title=General Relativity and John Archibald Wheeler|last2=Matzner|first2=Richard A.|date=22 June 2010|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-90-481-3735-0|language=en}}</ref> with the adoption of a three resonant mode configuration the design of which was led by Vitale.

=== The LISA Pathfinder and LISA missions ===
In 2003 Vitale became the Principal Investigator of the LISA Technology Package, the sole instrument of the [[LISA Pathfinder]] mission of the European Space Agency. LISA Pathfinder was the precursor to the space-based GW detector LISA ([[Laser Interferometer Space Antenna]]), under development by ESA and [[NASA]]. LISA Pathfinder operated between 2015 and 2017, and successfully demonstrated the viability of the planned LISA Mission.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Armano|first1=M.|last2=Audley|first2=H.|last3=Baird|first3=J.|last4=Binetruy|first4=P.|last5=Born|first5=M.|last6=Bortoluzzi|first6=D.|last7=Castelli|first7=E.|last8=Cavalleri|first8=A.|last9=Cesarini|first9=A.|last10=Cruise|first10=A. M.|last11=Danzmann|first11=K.|date=5 February 2018|title=Beyond the Required LISA Free-Fall Performance: New LISA Pathfinder Results down to $20\text{ }\text{ }\ensuremath{\mu}\mathrm{Hz}$|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=120|issue=6|article-number=061101|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.061101|pmid=29481269|doi-access=free|hdl=10044/1/57430|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Vitale led the design of the gravity reference sensor and the overall design of the experiment. LISA Pathfinder was decommissioned in July 2017<ref>{{Cite news|date=18 July 2017|title=LISA Pathfinder: Time called on Europe's gravity probe|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-40644104|access-date=2021-10-01}}</ref> and the post of Principal Investigator duly expired in 2018.

Vitale is a member of the core international scientific team behind LISA, serving both within international scientific team for several years and on the executive committee of the LISA consortium. From 2016 to 2017 he was Co-Principal Investigator of LISA and since 2020 he is Co-Lead of the LISA Consortium. The LISA Consortium is a large international collaboration<ref>{{Cite web|title=LISA Consortium {{!}} Lisamission.org|url=https://www.lisamission.org/articles/lisa-consortium|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.lisamission.org}}</ref> that combines the resources and expertise from scientists in many countries all over the world. Together with ESA and NASA, the LISA Consortium is working to bring the LISA Mission to fruition.  

== Awards and honours ==

* Asteroid N 19331, of IAU Catalogue of Minor Planets, has been named Stefanovitale (2016)<ref>{{Cite web|last=The International Astronomical Union Minor Planets Center|date=30 September 2021|title=Minor Planet Names: Alphabetical List|url=https://minorplanetcenter.net/iau/lists/MPNames.html#S|access-date=2021-10-06|website=minorplanetcenter.net}}</ref>
* As a member of LISA Pathfinder team, the ESA Corporate Team Achievement Award (2017)
* As a member of LISA Pathfinder team, the 2017 Space Technology Award of the [[American Astronautical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology – LISA Pathfinder wins American Astronautical Society award|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/lisa-pathfinder/-/59943-lisa-pathfinder-wins-american-astronautical-society-award|access-date=2021-10-05|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref>
* Amaldi Medal (European Prize for Gravitation of the Italian Gravitation Society) (2018)<ref>{{Cite web|date=28 June 2018|title=Professor Stefano Vitale Awarded Two Prizes|url=https://webmagazine.unitn.it/en/news/ateneo/43150/professor-stefano-vitale-awarded-two-prizes|access-date=2021-10-01|website=webmagazine.unitn.it|language=en}}</ref>
* [[Tycho Brahe Medal]] of the [[European Astronomical Society]] (2020)<ref>{{Cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |title=European Astronomical Society 2020 Prizes |url=https://eas.unige.ch/documents/eas_prizes_2020.pdf |publisher=European Astronomical Society |date=2020 |access-date=2026-10-12}}</ref>
